subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should OpenClaw add a privileged high-priority system-event path, and should it bypass heartbeat/session lanes or use a typed notification/admin alert surface instead?
rationale: Current main intentionally defers heartbeat/system-event wakes when command or session lanes are active; bypassing that changes trusted prompt injection, delivery ordering, abuse controls, and session-state safety.

options.title: Design explicit priority wake contract
options.body: Define auth, sanitization, rate-limit, ordering, and session-safety rules, then implement a narrow priority system-event path with tests.

options.title: Use notification surface instead
options.body: Make the connected-UI notification work the canonical urgent-alert path and leave prompt-stream system events heartbeat-mediated.

options.title: Keep best-effort heartbeat semantics
options.body: Document that in-session system events can be delayed under saturated lanes and rely on external channels for outage alerts.

recommendation.title: Design explicit priority wake contract
recommendation.body: Define auth, sanitization, rate-limit, ordering, and session-safety rules, then implement a narrow priority system-event path with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway wake behavior, system-event delivery, CLI surface, and security/session-state policy where this account has the strongest current ownership signal.
